integration_questions: With wheel_radius 0.040 m and wheel_track 0.10 m, does steering_oscillation on the oval stay near 0.2, or does the higher speed add jitter?
Does the slalom progress move past the 0.17 to 0.18 plateau? If not, is the stall a speed limit or a controller reaction-time limit?
Does s-bend progress hold near 0.49? If it drops, the radius-to-track ratio is the likely cause, and the next step is to return to 0.035 m radius with 0.09 m track.
Does control_effort stay near 7 to 8, and do line_loss_events stay near 1 per run on the bend entries?

intent: Test whether higher ground speed (wheel_radius 0.035 to 0.040 m) lifts the slalom plateau, with wheel_track widened to 0.10 m so the radius-to-track ratio stays near the best-evidenced value. All sensor values stay at the iteration 4 best. Expected: slalom progress above 0.2, s-bend progress at or above 0.45, oval still finishing 18 to 20 of 20, and a faster completion time than 1.73 s.
learning: Iteration 6 showed footprint 0.016 m collapses the oval, and iteration 7 showed 0.008 m keeps the oval but hurts the s-bend, so 0.012 m is the sensing optimum. Iteration 5 showed narrowing the track to 0.08 m hurts the s-bend, so turn authority is near its optimum at 0.09 m for radius 0.035 m. Slalom progress has not moved with any sensing or turn-rate change, which points at speed as the next limit. If this radius increase lifts slalom progress without losing the s-bend, keep it and try a further radius step or a lower mass for acceleration. If it hurts the s-bend or oval, return to radius 0.035 m and treat the slalom as a controller-side limit to pass to the Integrator.
rationale: Evidence across eight iterations. The best design is still iteration 4 (score 404.6): 5 sensors at y=0.08 m, 0.015 m pitch, 0.012 m footprint, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg. It finishes 20/20 on the oval, with s-bend progress 0.486 and slalom progress 0.177. Two sensor-footprint tests bracket the 0.012 m choice. At 0.016 m the oval collapsed to 0/20 (score 72.5). At 0.008 m the oval held at 20/20, but s-bend progress fell to 0.32 and the score dropped to 383.9. So 0.012 m stays. Wheel track is also tuned: 0.08 m cut s-bend progress to 0.33 and 0.10 m (iteration 1, at y=0.07) was weaker than 0.09 m. The s-bend limit appears to depend on the ratio of wheel_radius to wheel_track, since yaw rate scales with wheel speed over track and wheel speed scales with radius. The slalom has stalled at progress 0.16 to 0.18 across every design tried (iterations 1, 3, 4, 5, 7), whatever the track, row position or footprint. Sensing and turn-rate levers look exhausted, so the untested lever is ground speed. The contract's speed relation (wheel_radius times rotation rate) and the 3 s finish limit (about 1.5 m/s average needed) both point at the wheel radius. Radius scales both top speed and turn rate, so I raise wheel_radius from 0.035 to 0.040 m and widen wheel_track from 0.09 to 0.10 m. That keeps the radius-to-track ratio near 0.40, close to the 0.389 that gave the best s-bend result, so the turn authority should stay similar while ground speed rises about 14 percent. Everything else stays at the iteration 4 values, so the effect is isolated. Expected result: a faster completion time (up to about 60 score points from the time term), slalom progress above 0.2, and s-bend progress at or near 0.49. Main risk: higher speed could push the bends off track, and the Integrator should check max_error and line_loss_events first.
